15.0.0.en: The land of your habitations: that is, the land of Canaan, which will be given to the people.

15.0.1.en: After the punishment of the people and their turning once again toward the wilderness and the Red Sea, God begins His speech with Moses anew, renewing to them His promise to bring them into this land, and He affirms that He will give it to them in the end despite the many peoples who dwell in it. After punishing them, He returns and encourages them that He will bring them in, that is, will bring their children, into the land of Canaan. These are the laws which they will fulfill there, where they will sow the land and have wheat, oil and wine in abundance, since in the wilderness they had been living on manna and did not sow.

15.1.0.en: Make an offering by fire unto the LORD: an expression meaning “offer your sacrifices to the Lord.”

15.1.1.en: Freewill offering: a voluntary sacrifice offered as an expression of love for God.

15.1.2.en: This verse is an introduction to verses 4-11. In this verse He begins by mentioning the kinds of animals offered in the various sacrifices, as a preparation for the accompanying offerings that would be required of them with these sacrifices.

15.2.1.en: The fourth part of an hin: 0.950 liter.

15.2.2.en: Everyone who offers the animal of the sacrifice, his “offering,” to God before the tabernacle must also offer a “tenth deal” of flour mingled with oil, and the amount of oil with which the flour is mingled is the fourth part of an hin. As for the wine that was poured on the sacrifice or the altar, its measure is also the fourth part of an hin.

15.2.3.en: Note: the purpose of these offerings was to teach the people the following:

15.2.4.en: 1- That everything we offer to God is from the good with which He has blessed us.

15.2.5.en: 2- The pouring out of wine signifies joy, and God accepts nothing from a man unless he offers it to God with joy of heart.

15.2.6.en: 3- Wine also signifies the blood of Christ, which was shed on the wood of the Cross and gave salvation to the whole world.

15.2.7.en: 4- The pouring out of wine also signifies the giving of sweat and blood and striving in order to enjoy salvation and the Kingdom of Heaven.

15.3.0.en: The previous offering accompanied the ordinary lamb. As for the ram, which is the large male sheep distinguished by its large horns, the offerings accompanying it, of fine flour mingled with oil and wine poured out, were somewhat more: the flour became double and the drink offering became a third part instead of a fourth.

15.4.0.en: If the sacrifice is a bullock, that is, a son of the herd, the flour offering is increased to three tenth deals and the wine offering to half an hin.

15.4.1.en: Offering made by fire: an indication that these offerings are offered on the altar.

15.4.2.en: A sweet savour: that is, what a man offers to the Lord with pleasure, God also accepts with pleasure and favor.

15.5.0.en: These two verses come as a review of all the preceding verses concerning the earlier offerings. He returns and mentions the names of the animals again and affirms that each sacrifice has its own offerings, which usually correspond to its size.

15.6.0.en: God makes the native, that is, the one of Hebrew origin, equal to the stranger in the offering, for the offering to God is not tied to nationality or color but to the sacrifice, and this is a type of Christ, in whom all are equal. The stranger meant here is of two kinds:

15.6.1.en: 1) The mixed multitude: that is, the Egyptians who came out with the people from Egypt.

15.6.2.en: 2) “Among you”: that is, the peoples who lived among them, such as the Gibeonites in the days of Joshua the son of Nun, with whom peace treaties were made, and who intermarried with the people and became part of them.

15.7.0.en: These two verses are a review and confirmation of what preceded, that the law of the preceding offerings is an everlasting and eternal law, from which neither the stranger nor the guest is excepted.

15.7.1.en: The idea of offerings and gifts to God has been dwindling in people's minds, since everyone is content with tithes only. But when we offer more than the tithes with joy, what we offer is a sweet savour presented to God, and He accepts it with joy... And do not forget that everything we offer is from the gifts of God to us.

15.8.0.en: God renews His speech to the people, as He did in (v. 2), about the laws that follow after their dwelling in the land which He will give them. The expression “when ye eat of the bread of the land” means that they had settled, sown the land and reaped it, and had wheat and flour from which they made their own bread, and therefore they had to heave, that is, to offer to the Lord, a “heave” offering.

15.9.0.en: This offering was that a man should offer to God the first cake of dough that he had leavened for making wine.

15.9.1.en: The threshingfloor: the place where the wheat is separated from the ears.

15.9.2.en: What is meant is that the first quantity of wheat to come out of the threshingfloor, enough to make a cake of bread, a man must take, grind and knead, and offer as a firstfruit directly from the floor to God before taking bread for himself.

15.10.0.en: Here He affirms the importance of offering firstfruits. In this verse God repeats to them the necessity of offering the first of the dough to the Lord, and the priests and their households used to eat it (Neh 10:37).

15.10.1.en: If you feel that everything you receive in life is a gift from God, it is natural that you should share with God in enjoying these gifts by offering Him their firstfruits, so that His needy brethren may rejoice with you.

15.11.s.en: (3) The offering of sacrifices for sins of ignorance and of presumption

15.11.0.en: Ye have erred: you have forgotten, or your failure was unintentional.

15.11.1.en: God speaks to the people through Moses, telling them that if a failure should occur on the part of the whole people in any of the commandments or laws of worship that God gave to the people, and this was because of forgetfulness and not on purpose, then they must hold to everything that follows, throughout all their generations, to atone for this error (see Lev 4). From the day that the LORD commanded: that is, since you received the commandments and the laws.

15.12.0.en: Ignorantly: without the knowledge of the congregation.

15.12.1.en: Of course the people had to make amends for this error, even if it was by oversight or unintentional, so the people offer from their possessions two sacrifices, one of them a sin offering, which is a he-goat, that is, a male goat. When the sin offering is offered and God accepts their amends, they then offer a burnt offering, which is a bullock, for a sweet savour to God, as a collective gift from the people to the Lord.

15.12.2.en: Note: the bullock is mentioned before the he-goat, perhaps because of its higher price than the goat, but the goat was offered first, for the due apology comes before the gift of reconciliation.

15.12.3.en: When we sin it is not enough to offer our apology to God only in words, or merely to abstain from sin, but we must also grow in virtue and the spiritual life, such as prayer and reading the Holy Bible.

15.13.0.en: When the people did this, that is, offered the sin offering and the burnt offering, God forgave them their sin and made allowance for them because this sin was by oversight. The compassionate God has pity on and takes account of human weakness, but man must offer repentance and apology in all cases. God makes clear that His forgiveness and pardon include all the people, the Hebrews and also the rebellious strangers who dwell with them or who came out with them from the land of Egypt.

15.13.1.en: An offering made by fire unto the LORD: the expression “made by fire” is used with the burnt offering only because it was burned entirely as a sweet savour to the Lord.

15.13.2.en: Second: the sin of ignorance of the individual:

15.14.0.en: A she goat of the first year: that is, a year old.

15.14.1.en: But if one person falls into a sin of ignorance, and not the whole people, he too must draw near to God with repentance in order to atone for his sin, so he offers a sacrifice of redemption for himself from the mature goats (a year old). The atonement took place by taking the blood of the sacrifice and pouring it out at the bottom of the altar to be burned, which is a clear indication of the blood of Christ shed on the Cross, without which no atonement for man's sins takes place (see Lev 4). God did not except the stranger sojourning among the people from this law, and there is a beautiful spiritual meaning in this: when a guest comes to stay with one of us, we should not indulge him at God's expense, but rather he should submit to our order, our prayers and our fasts, and we should encourage him to do so, instead of our being led along with him.

15.15.0.en: Doeth ought with an high hand: that is, commits its sin deliberately.

15.15.1.en: God in His justice distinguishes between what a man does by oversight or from human weakness, on the one hand, and the evil he commits with audacity, full will and prior planning, that is, premeditation, on the other. God regards deliberate sins as a direct contempt of His holy person and of His word and commandments, and therefore the punishment here is proportionate to the offense and also severe: the punishment was cutting off. Cutting off here means that this person is set apart and driven out from the congregation of the people, and his fate is in the hand of God according to His wisdom and judgment. To show the gravity of the offense, God affirms a second time, “shall utterly be cut off,” and that the iniquity of this soul is upon him, the one who committed his sin with awareness and full planning.

15.15.2.en: We do not know what happened afterward, whether this soul was received again if it repented or not, but the story of the prophet David assures us that God does not reject a repentant heart forever but receives it with His wide mercies. There is no sin without forgiveness except the one without repentance. But we must also guard with all care against despising the dignity of the holy God by doing evil with indifference or deliberately.

15.16.0.en: Right after the speech about sins of presumption and what they represent of contempt for God and disdain or disregard of His commandment, an incident comes here that confirms that God does not tolerate the deliberate sinner. The divine inspiration here tells us the story of a man who broke the commandment of the Sabbath and did not sanctify it, for he went out of his tent and began gathering and breaking up some sticks on the Sabbath day.

15.17.1.en: When some of the people saw that, they took him and brought him to Moses and Aaron before all the people. Since Moses and Aaron did not know what to do with him, because this was the first time a man had broken a Sabbath, they put him in confinement so that Moses might have the opportunity to ask the Lord about him.

15.17.2.en: Ask God's counsel before any work, however great your experience or position, as Moses did not rely on his own understanding but asked God. Then God will guide you, bless you and protect you from many troubles.

15.18.0.en: When Moses asked the Lord, the punishment came decisive and deterrent. The sentence was that he be put to death by stoning outside the camp, and that all the people take part in stoning him.

15.18.1.en: In this incident the following is noticed:

15.18.2.en: 1- There was no injustice in the punishment, for the man broke one of the important Ten Commandments and so deserved the punishment.

15.18.3.en: 2- This man insulted the dignity of God, did not care about obeying Him, and departed from the custom of all the people of his nation.

15.18.4.en: 3- He did not learn from the previous punishments that God brought on His people when they disobeyed.

15.18.5.en: 4- He did not heed the previous warning that every soul that commits sin deliberately is cut off from its people.

15.18.6.en: 5- He was extremely brazen and impudent, for he dared to commit this sin in the middle of the day.

15.18.7.en: 6- The punishment had to be a deterrent so that all the people would fear and such an event would not be repeated, and the people would learn that God is jealous for His glory.

15.19.0.en: In great fear and awe the people obeyed God's command and carried out the punishment on this man. It was a lesson no one forgets and a practical teaching that the days do not erase, that God's commandments must be respected, and that despising them means death and destruction.

15.20.s.en: (5) Making fringes and ribbons for garments

15.20.0.en: After one of the people dared to despise God and broke the Sabbath, forgetting His commandment, God asked Moses to command the people to make a memorial set before their eyes that would make them always remember the divine commandments. This memorial was as follows:

15.20.1.en: Fringes: a group of threads forming a tuft, like the button of a tarboosh, or what is called in colloquial speech (tassels). Borders: ends.

15.20.2.en: Ribband: a band placed above the fringes, blue in color, one of whose purposes is to fasten these fringes.

15.20.3.en: God asked the people to be committed to making fringes on the borders of their garments, and these fringes hang from a piece of cloth of the color sky-blue, that is, blue, as a symbol that the various laws and commandments, “the fringes,” have their source in the blue heaven and that the whole Law is heavenly.

15.21.0.en: The purpose on seeing these fringes is to remember the heavenly Law and that a man's eyes should stay on God's commandments, so that his heart does not stray after its desires to the right and to the left, and likewise the eyes are fixed on the divine commandments and see nothing but God and His judgments.

15.21.1.en: God uses material memorials so that we do not forget His teachings. He reminds His children of the pot of manna and the Passover and many things so that they do not forget His work with them, and He still reminds us in the New Testament through the rites of the Church so that we abide in His love. But unfortunately some are occupied with appearance rather than essence, like the Pharisees, who cared for these ribbons and fringes and left the love of God and mercy, and Christ rebuked them (Mt 23:4, 5).

15.22.0.en: As a result of a man's eyes being fixed on the commandments and his zeal to fulfill them and to please the heart of God, he becomes holy and set apart for God.

15.23.0.en: At the end of God's speech with His people, He reminds them that He is their only God, who loosed their captivity and brought them out of the land of Egypt with a strong arm to be a God to them and that they be a people to Him, but on condition of their holiness and their remembering His commandments.

15.23.1.en: Note: Jews in many parts of the world still wear these fringes, whether on religious occasions or in their daily life. They wrap their waists (their loins) with a piece of light blue cloth ending in these fringes, to declare their adherence to the commandments of their God.

15.23.2.en: My beloved brother, the Cross has become for us a memorial set before our eyes that reminds us not only of God's commandments but of His love and redemption of us all... Set your eyes on the Cross and you will receive help and strength from your remembering the love of Christ for you, so that sin will not prevail over you and will have no authority over you, but you will tread it down with the authority of the children of God.

15.23.3.en: The murmuring of Korah, Dathan and Abiram
